newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels claim capture of border town.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels claim capture of border town.

text.p: Sudan People's Liberation Army spokesman Yassir Said Arman said in Eritrea the SPLA on Sunday captured the town of Kurmuk on the Sudan-Ethiopia border.
"The forces of the SPLA managed to capture the town of Kurmuk as well as Gazan and Gova in the southern Blue Nile region," Arman told Reuters.
Kurmuk is south of Damazine, which the SPLA spokesman said is a main source of electrical power in Sudan. Arman said the fighting over Kurmuk lasted five hours, but he had no details.
"The forces of the SPLA are advancing towards Damazine, which is a key centre of production of electric power in Sudan. We are already beyond Kurmuk," Arman told Reuters.
He said another military operation was carried out at the same time by a joint force of the umbrella opposition group, the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).

"The joint force of the NDA under the joint military command composed of the Umma Party, the DUP (Democratic Unionist Party), the SAF (Sudan Alliance Forces) and the Tana Brigade of the SPLA, managed to capture the army garrisons at Yakru, Agtura and Manssa in the northern Blue Nile area. Those forces managed to destroy four Sudan army brigades," Arman said.
The Sudan opposition's joint force was formed last October following opposition leadership meetings at the NDA headquarters in the Eritrean capital, Asmara.
The joint force, with SPLA's John Garang as commander, includes forces from most Sudanese opposition groups.
